source.title: A Boundary-Layer Mechanism for One-Third Scaling in Online Softmax Classification
source.authors: Marcel Kühn; Yoon Thelge; Bernd Rosenow

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure labels and equations are flattened, but the main theoretical results and relevant text are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests power-law behavior in online classification and extends it to image-related settings, but it does not sweep language-model parameters, tokens, or compute or test compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The study primarily measures loss and classification error against online training time, not against parameter count, training tokens, or training compute. It reports no compute-optimal parameter/token split. Results cited from other work are not recorded as findings. Pythia token top-1 error is not a downstream-task measure, and its Pythia loss-curve reproduction is not reported here with an outcome that tests the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly a solvable toy-model theory of training-time power laws. Its empirical checks bear on two versions. For V5, a MNIST MLP and a linear readout on ViT image features show power-law test loss and error versus online training time in image classification. For V7, Pythia fit exponents are reported as sensitive to the choice of fit window. It does not sweep parameters, tokens or compute for language models, and it tests no compute-optimal split.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors derive a boundary-layer mechanism giving α^−1/3 laws for both test loss and error in online softmax classification. The error law comes from online SGD noise, while the loss law persists without that noise. Annealing raises the error exponent toward 1/2 while slowing the loss. Correlated and whitened-feature inputs change transients but not the late-time decay, MNIST is compatible with one-third, and Pythia 12B top-1 error is compatible with 1/3. They frame the mechanism as asymptotic and complementary to spectral explanations.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives and simulates online teacher–student classification dynamics, then tests selected image and language-model settings. It does not reproduce the parameter/token/compute sweeps or compute-optimal allocation methods of the original scaling-law studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate schedule changes the theoretical time exponents; increasing covariance anisotropy lengthens transients; smaller learning rates can delay asymptotic entry; Pythia fit-window edge shifts materially affect fitted exponents.

fits_no_version.finding: In the solvable online softmax teacher-student model, test loss and error both decay as α^−1/3 at fixed learning rate. Without gradient noise, the loss keeps this law but the error decays faster than any power.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time power laws in hard-label classification can arise from decision-boundary geometry, with the error exponent set by online SGD noise.

fits_no_version.finding: For Pythia, token top-1 error above a fitted floor follows a power law in a heuristic residual-aware time. Exponents are 0.463 (410M), 0.422 (2.8B) and 0.365 (12B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time exponents of token top-1 error at fixed model size vary with model size and fit window.

fits_no_version.finding: Correlated-Gaussian inputs lengthen transients without changing the late-time exponent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input covariance structure affects crossover timing rather than the asymptotic training-time exponent in boundary-layer dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Zipf aggregation over sub-tasks gives a total error exponent of min{1/3, 1−1/ν}, so heavy-tailed data masks the per-task exponent. This is a theoretical scaling argument.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Observed aggregate exponents can depend on the data frequency tail rather than on the underlying learning mechanism.

record.problems: The main theory assumes a one-layer fixed-feature model, Gaussian inputs, noiseless hard labels, online SGD, and a thermodynamic limit. The image-feature results are described as controlled departures, not a theorem for arbitrary features; real-label runs hit a floor early. The Pythia fit uses a heuristic time coordinate, and fitted exponents are sensitive to fit-window choices. Several numerical values are available only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted for the 60-row limit. Cited results from other studies and Pythia loss-curve outcomes without a reported result in this paper were not entered as rows.

untested.parts: No language-model sweep over parameters, tokens or compute. The Pythia loss-curve reproduction is mentioned but no outcomes are reported.
No extrapolation from small runs to large ones.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed size.
Only image classification, as training time at fixed model size. Not tested: video, repeated-data laws, transfer, and scaling with model size or compute.
No downstream-task measure; Pythia token top-1 error is not a downstream task.
Not tested: parameter-counting conventions, the compute-optimal split, and fitting method beyond the fit window. The schedule dependence is shown only in a toy model.

missing.what: Per-model Pythia exponents with asymmetric uncertainties are given in the legend but missing from the R15 and R16 values.
The Zipf sub-task aggregation result, an exponent masking argument, has no row.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling variable throughout is online training time (fresh samples) at fixed model size, never model size or compute. The V7 support from R4–R7 comes from a toy model; the support from R18 is qualitative. The text says the Pythia loss curves of Liu et al. were reproduced and confirmed, but reports no numbers.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model parameters, training tokens, or compute; the reported scaling variable is online training time.
No small-run fits are used to predict substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameter count and token count is tested.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests image-classification settings, not video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer; does not test power laws over parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No downstream-task performance prediction from scale or pretraining loss. Pythia token top-1 error is a next-token measure, not a downstream-task measure.

Tests sensitivity of time-scaling exponents to learning-rate schedules and Pythia fit-window choices, but not parameter-count conventions, compute-optimal allocation, or bending of loss curves versus model scale.
